name: Wall
description: Draws a wall along a sketched path or picked line, hosting doors, windows and hosted fittings as you place them. The workhorse of any Revit model — reach for it whenever you are blocking out enclosure or partitions, then swap the type later as the design firms up.

name: Door
description: Places a door family into a host wall, cutting its opening automatically and flipping swing direction with the spacebar. Use it early to test circulation, since doors schedule and tag themselves as the model grows.

name: Window
description: Inserts a window family into a wall, cutting the opening and inheriting sill height from the type. Handy for rapid facade studies because instances can be retyped in bulk from the Properties palette.

name: Column (Architectural)
description: Places a non-structural column used for boxing out casings, decorative piers or coordination placeholders. It merges with walls of the same material, unlike a structural column which carries analytical data.

name: Structural Column
description: Places a load-bearing column, usually snapped to grid intersections, with an analytical stick for engineering exchange. Use At Grids placement to populate a whole frame in one action.

name: Beam
description: Draws a structural framing member between supports, picking up level and work plane automatically. Reach for it when coordinating with engineers or roughing out an exposed structure that the architecture must wrap around.

name: Brace
description: Adds a diagonal framing member between two points, typically drawn in elevation or section between levels. Used for lateral systems and for modelling visible cross-bracing in exposed frames.

name: Isolated Foundation
description: Places a pad or pile-cap foundation family beneath columns. Useful for early coordination of footing sizes against basement walls and drainage.

name: Floor
description: Creates a floor slab from a closed sketched boundary on the current level, with build-up defined by the floor type. Edit the sketch at any time to chase openings, balconies or slab steps as plans change.

name: Ceiling
description: Generates a ceiling either automatically inside bounding walls or from a sketch, at a set offset from the level. Model ceilings before lighting layouts so hosted fittings have something to land on in reflected ceiling plans.

name: Roof by Footprint
description: Builds a roof from a plan sketch, with slope arrows or per-edge slope settings generating hips and valleys automatically. The quickest route to conventional pitched or flat roofs that follow the building outline.

name: Roof by Extrusion
description: Creates a roof by extruding a profile sketched in elevation or section, ideal for barrel vaults, sawtooth and other section-driven shapes a footprint roof cannot describe. Walls can then attach to its underside.

name: Stair
description: Assembles a stair from runs, landings and supports, checking riser counts against the level-to-level height as you go. Use component-based runs for standard flights and sketch editing for irregular geometry.

name: Railing
description: Sketches a railing along a path or places it on a stair or ramp host so it follows the slope. Balusters, rails and posts all come from the type, so build the type once and reuse it across the project.

name: Ramp
description: Creates an inclined ramp between levels from run and landing sketches, with maximum slope and length governed by the type. Use it for step-free access studies where gradients must be proven, not just drawn.

name: Curtain Grid
description: Adds gridlines to a curtain wall or curtain system, subdividing it into panels that mullions can then follow. Use it to override the automatic type-driven spacing where a facade needs a bespoke rhythm.

name: Mullion
description: Places mullion profiles onto curtain gridlines, either one segment at a time or across all gridlines at once. Swap the profile type to move between chunky concept framing and a specific system supplier look.

name: Curtain System
description: Applies a panelised curtain grid to selected faces of a mass or generic model, useful for glazing doubly-curved or faceted surfaces where a standard curtain wall cannot flex. Update the mass and regenerate to keep the skin in step.

name: Model Line
description: Draws a 3D line that lives in model space on a chosen work plane, visible in every view that can see it. Use it for setting-out geometry, railing paths or design intent lines that must exist in three dimensions, unlike detail lines.

name: Model Text
description: Creates extruded 3D text placed on a work plane, for signage, engraving or building names that must appear in renders and elevations. It is real geometry, so use annotation text for anything that is purely drawing content.

name: Component
description: Places a loadable family instance — furniture, sanitaryware, equipment, entourage — from the families already in the project. Pair it with Load Family when the piece you need is not yet available in the type selector.

name: In-Place Component
description: Starts a family modelled directly in the project context using extrusions, blends and sweeps, for one-off geometry tied to its surroundings. Use it sparingly — in-place families do not repeat efficiently, so promote anything reused to a loadable family.

name: Grid
description: Draws a numbered grid datum that appears in every plan, section and elevation it crosses, giving the project its structural setting-out. Place columns At Grids and dimension to gridlines so coordination survives design churn.

name: Level
description: Creates a horizontal datum that hosts floors, walls and views, drawn in a section or elevation. Every storey-driven element measures itself from a level, so name and order levels carefully before modelling begins in earnest.

name: Reference Plane
description: Draws an infinite construction plane you can name, work-plane onto and dimension against. The backbone of disciplined family building and a quick way to hold key setting-out lines in the project.

name: Set Work Plane
description: Chooses the plane that subsequent sketching and placement will land on — a level, a named reference plane or a picked face. Essential when modelling on sloped or vertical surfaces where the default level plane is wrong.

name: Room
description: Places a room element that fills the space bounded by walls and room separation lines, carrying name, number, area and finishes data. Rooms drive schedules and colour fills, so place them as soon as plans are stable enough to name.

name: Room Separator
description: Draws a room separation line that bounds rooms where no wall exists, such as splitting an open-plan floor into named zones. Keep them tidy — stray separators are a classic cause of mysterious room boundaries.

name: Area
description: Places an area element in an area plan for measurement schemes independent of rooms — gross internal, lettable, planning use classes. Use it when the measurement rules differ from how rooms are actually bounded.

name: Area Boundary
description: Sketches the lines that bound areas in an area plan, either picked from walls or drawn freely. Because they are independent of walls, you can measure to whatever convention the brief demands.

name: Shaft Opening
description: Cuts a vertical shaft through multiple floors, roofs and ceilings between a base and top level in one element. The right tool for lift shafts, risers and atria, because the cut follows the sketch through every storey it spans.

name: Wall Opening
description: Cuts a rectangular opening in a straight or curved wall without placing a door or window family. Useful for pass-throughs, service penetrations and openings that should not appear in door or window schedules.

name: Duct
description: Draws rigid ductwork with automatic fittings between points, sized and system-typed as you go. Architects mostly meet it when checking ceiling void clearances against MEP models, but it is handy for quick in-house coordination studies.

name: Pipe
description: Routes piping with fittings and slope control between connectors or free points. Useful for sanity-checking drainage falls and riser space before the engineer's model arrives.

name: Toposolid
description: Models the site terrain as a solid with real thickness and layers, created from a sketch, imported CAD contours or a points file. It replaced the old toposurface, so cut-and-fill, sub-bases and excavations behave like proper geometry.

name: Site Component
description: Places site families — trees, benches, bollards — that host themselves onto the toposolid at the correct elevation. Use it for entourage that should follow the terrain rather than sit at a fixed level.

name: Place Mass
description: Inserts a loadable conceptual mass family for early volumetric studies, with floor area schedules driven by mass floors. Later, walls, roofs and curtain systems can be generated from its faces so the concept flows into the detailed model.

name: In-Place Mass
description: Sketches a conceptual mass directly in the project using profiles, forms and voids, ideal for site-specific volume studies against neighbouring context. Convert faces to walls, floors and roofs once a scheme is chosen.

name: Modify
description: Returns the cursor to the default selection arrow, ending whatever placement or sketch tool is active. Tapping Escape twice does the same job, but the shortcut is a reliable way to bail out of a mode cleanly.

name: Move
description: Relocates the selection by picking two points or typing a distance, with constrain and disjoin options on the ribbon. Prefer it over dragging for anything that must land precisely, and remember hosted elements move with their host.

name: Copy
description: Duplicates the selection from one picked point to another, with a Multiple option for repeated placement. This is the in-view copy — use Copy to Clipboard instead when the target is another level or another view.

name: Rotate
description: Spins the selection about a centre point, which you can drag to a new position before picking or typing the angle. Tick Copy on the options bar to leave the original in place.

name: Mirror - Pick Axis
description: Reflects the selection about an existing line, wall face or reference plane you pick. The fastest mirror when the axis already exists in the model, such as a party wall between handed flats.

name: Mirror - Draw Axis
description: Reflects the selection about a temporary axis you sketch on the fly. Reach for it when no convenient line exists to mirror about — the drawn axis vanishes once the command completes.

name: Array
description: Creates a linear or radial array of the selection, optionally grouped and associated so changing the count later updates every member. Ideal for repetitive bays, balusters or hotel rooms where the repeat may still change.

name: Align
description: Snaps an element flush to a reference you pick first — face to gridline, window to window, edge to edge — with an optional padlock to keep them constrained. One of the most powerful precision tools in Revit; many users reach for it before Move.

name: Trim/Extend to Corner
description: Joins two walls or lines into a clean corner, trimming or extending each as needed — click the portions you want to keep. The everyday clean-up tool while sketching plans and profiles.

name: Trim/Extend Single Element
description: Extends or trims one element to meet a boundary reference you pick first. Use it to run a partition to the underside of a corridor wall line without disturbing anything else.

name: Trim/Extend Multiple Elements
description: Trims or extends a whole series of elements to a single boundary, picked one after another or fenced with a crossing selection. A big time-saver when squaring up many partitions to one datum wall.

name: Split Element
description: Cuts a wall, line or pipe into two independent pieces at the point you click, with an option to delete the inner segment between two clicks. Split walls where the type, phase or height changes along a run.

name: Split with Gap
description: Splits a wall and leaves a defined joint gap between the two halves, keeping them dimensionally related. Made for movement joints and panelised construction where a real break is required.

name: Offset
description: Creates a copy of a line or wall at a set distance to one side, or moves it there if Copy is unticked. Set the distance on the options bar first, then hover to preview which side the offset will fall.

name: Scale
description: Resizes lines, imported CAD or reference planes graphically or by a numeric factor. Most building elements refuse to scale by design — sizes belong to types — so its main use is correcting imported drawings at the wrong units.

name: Pin
description: Locks the selection so it cannot be moved or deleted without deliberately unpinning first. Pin grids, levels, links and setting-out geometry the moment they are agreed — it is cheap insurance against accidental nudges.

name: Unpin
description: Releases a pinned element so it can be edited or moved again. Unpin deliberately, make the change, then pin again — leaving datums unpinned invites trouble on shared models.

name: Delete
description: Removes the selected elements from the model. Watch the warnings — deleting a host or boundary element can silently take tags, dimensions and hosted families with it.

name: Match Type Properties
description: Copies the type from a source element onto others of the same category — pick the donor, then click each element to convert. Quick for harmonising wall or window types across a floor after a design change.

name: Paint
description: Applies a material to a single face without changing the element type, ideal for a feature wall or a contrasting soffit. Painted faces override the type material only on that face, so use Remove Paint to get back to the honest build-up.

name: Split Face
description: Divides a face of an element into regions with a sketched boundary, without splitting the element itself. Combine with Paint for wainscots, tiling zones and feature bands on a single wall.

name: Linework
description: Overrides the line style of individual model edges in the current view only — heavy up a profile, ghost a hidden edge, or use Invisible Lines to suppress a distracting edge. Purely graphical, so the model itself is untouched.

name: Join Geometry
description: Merges the geometry of two overlapping elements so they cut cleanly and share edges — walls into floors, beams into walls. Joined elements stop double-counting volume and lose the tell-tale line where they overlap.

name: Unjoin Geometry
description: Breaks a previous geometry join so the two elements return to independent, overlapping solids. Use it when a join produces the wrong cutting priority or blocks an edit you need to make.

name: Cut Geometry
description: Makes one solid cut another, such as a void family or mass carving an opening through a wall or floor. The instrument behind bespoke openings that standard hosted families cannot make.

name: Wall Joins
description: Edits how walls meet at a junction — butt, mitre or square off — and which wall wins the joint. Reach for it when a corner cleans up the wrong way in plan and dragging ends has not fixed it.

name: Create Similar
description: Starts the placement tool for a new element of exactly the same type as the one selected. Faster than hunting through the type selector when you can see an example of what you want on screen.

name: Create Group
description: Bundles the selection into a named group whose instances stay synchronised — edit one and all update. The standard tool for repeated flats, hotel rooms and bathroom layouts before considering links.

name: Edit Group
description: Opens a group for editing in place, with the rest of the model greyed out; finishing pushes the change to every instance. Add or remove members here rather than ungrouping and rebuilding.

name: Ungroup
description: Dissolves a group instance back into independent elements, leaving other instances intact. Use it when one repeat genuinely diverges from the rest and should stop updating with them.

name: Measure Between Two References
description: Reports the distance between two picked points or references as a temporary readout, with a chain option for running totals. Use it for quick checks; place a real dimension when the measurement needs to live on a drawing.

name: Copy to Clipboard
description: Copies the selection to the clipboard for pasting into another view, level or even another open project. The first half of the standard routine for duplicating a floor layout up the building.

name: Paste from Clipboard
description: Pastes clipboard contents into the current view for manual placement, then lets you fine-tune the position before finishing. Use the Paste Aligned variants instead when the copy must land in exactly the same plan position.

name: Paste Aligned to Selected Levels
description: Pastes copied elements onto one or more chosen levels in exactly the same plan position. The classic way to stack a typical floor through a tower in seconds.

name: Filter
description: Opens a checklist of the categories in your current selection so you can keep some and drop the rest — for example, keep only the walls from a crossing window. Indispensable for surgical edits in crowded views.

name: Select All Instances
description: Selects every instance of the chosen type, either in the current view or across the whole project. Powerful for global swaps and equally capable of global accidents — check the scope before you edit.

name: Aligned Dimension
description: Places a dimension parallel to the references it measures, stringing along multiple picks into a chain. The default dimension for architectural drawings, and the gateway to EQ constraints for equal spacing.

name: Linear Dimension
description: Places a dimension locked to the horizontal or vertical between picked points, regardless of the angle between them. Useful for orthogonal setting-out dimensions across skewed geometry.

name: Angular Dimension
description: Measures and annotates the angle between two references. Reach for it on splayed walls, fan-shaped plans and roof pitches shown in section.

name: Radial Dimension
description: Annotates the radius of a curved wall, arc or filleted edge. Pair with the diameter variant depending on how your office convention notes curves.

name: Spot Elevation
description: Places a level marker reading the real elevation of the point it touches — slab levels, ridge heights, external ground. Because it reads the model, it updates itself when the geometry moves.

name: Spot Coordinate
description: Annotates the north/east coordinates of a point relative to the shared or project coordinate system. Standard on setting-out drawings where the contractor needs survey-grade positions.

name: Spot Slope
description: Places an arrow or triangle annotation reading the slope of a face or edge, such as a ramp or roof pitch. It reports the modelled gradient, so it doubles as a compliance check.

name: Text
description: Places view-specific text with optional leaders, scaling with the view like all annotation. Use it for general notes — but prefer tags and keynotes wherever the note describes an element, so the data stays live.

name: Tag by Category
description: Places the appropriate tag for whatever element you click — door tag on a door, wall tag on a wall — reading its parameters live. Tags are reporters, not labels: edit the element and the tag follows.

name: Tag All Not Tagged
description: Tags every untagged element of chosen categories in the current view in one pass. Run it as a drawing-issue chore to catch the doors and windows nobody tagged along the way.

name: Room Tag
description: Places a tag reading a room's name, number and area. Rooms and their tags are separate elements — delete a tag and the room survives, ready to be re-tagged in any view.

name: Area Tag
description: Tags an area element in an area plan with its name and computed area. Use it on lettable-area and planning drawings where measurement schemes are being reported.

name: Multi-Category Tag
description: Places a single tag family that can annotate elements of different categories, usually reading a shared parameter. Useful for uniform reference bubbles across mixed equipment and furniture.

name: Material Tag
description: Tags the material of the face you click, reading its description from the material asset. Handy on details and elevations where finishes are called up directly from the model.

name: Keynote
description: Annotates an element with a code from the project keynote table, keeping specification references consistent across every sheet. Change the table entry once and every keynote referencing it updates.

name: Detail Line
description: Draws 2D linework that exists only in the current view, for embellishing details over the model. If a line should appear in other views too, use a model line instead — mixing them up is a classic drafting error.

name: Detail Component
description: Places a 2D detail family — DPC, blockwork coursing, flashing profiles — into the current view only. The backbone of hybrid detailing, where model geometry is dressed with drafted components.

name: Filled Region
description: Sketches a closed 2D region with a fill pattern, for hatching earth, existing fabric or poche in a single view. Boundary line styles are set per edge, so the outline can vary around the shape.

name: Masking Region
description: Draws a white-out region that hides whatever sits behind it in the view. Use it to blank clashing linework under a detail or to tidy an area an imported drawing has cluttered — sparingly, since it hides rather than fixes.

name: Insulation
description: Draws the standard batt insulation squiggle along a path at a set width, as view-specific detailing. Quicker and more consistent than drawing loops by hand in wall and roof details.

name: Revision Cloud
description: Sketches a cloud around amended content and assigns it to a revision from the project revision list, which then reports into sheet title blocks. The formal mechanism for tracking drawing issues after first publication.

name: Symbol
description: Places a 2D annotation symbol family — north arrows, break lines, accessibility symbols — that scales with the view. Use it for standard graphic symbols that carry no model data.

name: Color Fill Legend
description: Applies a colour scheme to rooms or areas in the view and places the matching key. The fastest way to turn plans into departmental, tenure or use-class diagrams that stay live as rooms change.

name: Link Revit
description: References another Revit model into the project — structure, MEP, adjacent buildings — kept live and reloaded as the other team issues updates. The standard architecture for multi-discipline coordination; pin links immediately after placing.

name: Link CAD
description: References a DWG or similar CAD file that reloads when the source changes, rather than embedding it. Prefer linking over importing for surveys and consultant drawings so stale geometry never gets baked into the model.

name: Link IFC
description: References an IFC model from another authoring platform into the project, translated on link and refreshed on reload. The openBIM route for coordinating with consultants who do not work in Revit.

name: Import CAD
description: Embeds a CAD file directly into the project with no live connection to the source. Use only when the drawing is genuinely static — imported DWGs bloat files and cannot be refreshed, so linking is usually wiser.

name: Image
description: Places a raster image into a 2D view, for scanned sketches, logos or context photos on sheets. Images are view-specific and managed from the same dialog as other raster assets.

name: Point Cloud
description: Links a laser-scan point cloud into the model as a snappable reference. The starting point for retrofit and heritage work, where existing fabric is modelled over the scan.

name: Load Family
description: Brings an RFA family file from disk or the content library into the project, ready for placement. If a loaded family already exists, Revit offers to overwrite it — the standard way to push family edits into a live project.

name: Manage Links
description: Central dialog for every linked file — reload, unload, repath or remove Revit, CAD, IFC and point cloud links. Check it whenever linked content looks stale or a link has lost its file path.

name: Visibility/Graphics
description: Opens the per-view control panel for what is visible and how it draws — category visibility, overrides, filters, links and worksets. The first place to look when something is missing from a view; also answers to the VV shortcut.

name: View Filters
description: Creates rule-based or selection-based filters that recolour, override or hide elements matching criteria — fire-rated walls in red, new work highlighted, and so on. Applied per view or baked into view templates for consistency.

name: Thin Lines
description: Toggles all lines to a uniform hairline on screen regardless of their printed weight. Turn it on for precise modelling, off to preview how the drawing will actually read when plotted.

name: Render
description: Produces a photorealistic still of the current 3D view using materials, lighting and sun settings. Fine for quick in-house imagery; most practices push to Twinmotion or other visualisation tools for polished work.

name: Default 3D View
description: Opens the project's orthographic 3D view, creating it if it does not yet exist. The everyday working view for orbiting the whole model — pair it with Section Box to focus on one part.

name: Camera
description: Places a perspective camera in plan by picking an eye point and target, creating a new perspective view. The tool for client-facing eye-level images and quick interior checks at true human height.

name: Walkthrough
description: Creates an animated camera path through the model by placing keyframes in plan, exportable as video. Useful for early massing and circulation fly-throughs without leaving Revit.

name: Section
description: Draws a section line in plan or elevation and generates the corresponding live section view, with a draggable depth. Sections are views of the same model, so every design change appears in them instantly.

name: Callout
description: Draws a callout bubble around part of a view and creates a new, larger-scale view of just that region, with the reference tag linking to its sheet. The standard route from general arrangement into detail.

name: Elevation
description: Places an elevation marker in plan whose arrows each generate a live elevation view. Used for building facades and, with interior markers, for room-by-room internal elevations.

name: Plan Views
description: Creates a new floor plan, ceiling plan, area plan or structural plan for a chosen level. Use it to add working or presentation plans for levels that already exist without duplicating an existing view.

name: Reflected Ceiling Plan
description: Creates a plan viewed upward at the ceiling, mirrored as if reflected, for lighting and ceiling layouts. Ceiling-hosted elements placed here land correctly on the ceilings modelled below the level above.

name: Area Plan
description: Creates a plan dedicated to an area scheme, where area boundaries and area elements live. Each measurement convention — gross, net, lettable — gets its own scheme and its own plans.

name: Drafting View
description: Creates a blank 2D view with no model behind it, for typical details, standard notes and imported legacy details. Because nothing is live, use it only for content that genuinely does not depend on the model.

name: Duplicate View
description: Copies a view as a plain duplicate, with detailing (annotation comes too) or as a dependent (a cropped child sharing the parent's annotation). The standard way to spin working views off issued drawings so mark-ups never pollute sheets.

name: Legend
description: Creates a legend view where symbolic representations of types — wall build-ups, door types, symbols — are assembled with notes. Uniquely, one legend can be placed on many sheets, making it ideal for standard keys.

name: Schedule/Quantities
description: Builds a live tabular view of any category — doors, rooms, walls — with chosen fields, filters, sorting and totals. Schedules are two-way: edit a value in the table and the model changes, which makes them powerful auditing tools.

name: Sheet
description: Creates a new drawing sheet from a title block family, ready to receive views, schedules and legends. Sheet number and name feed the title block and the project's drawing list automatically.

name: Place View
description: Drops a view onto the open sheet as a viewport, complete with its title and scale. Each model view can sit on only one sheet, so duplicate the view first if the same content is needed twice.

name: Guide Grid
description: Overlays an alignment grid on sheets so viewports land in the same position from sheet to sheet. Use one shared guide grid across a plan series to stop drawings jumping when flicked through.

name: Revisions
description: Manages the project revision sequence — numbering, descriptions, dates and issued status — that revision clouds and title blocks report. Set the scheme up before first issue so the audit trail is clean from day one.

name: Scope Box
description: Creates a named 3D box that controls the extents of datums and the crop of views assigned to it. On large or multi-wing buildings, scope boxes keep grids, levels and view crops consistent across dozens of views at once.

name: View Template
description: Applies a saved bundle of view settings — scale, visibility, filters, graphics — to views, either once or as a locked assignment. The backbone of consistent drawing output: set standards in the template, not view by view.

name: Tile Views
description: Arranges all open views side by side so you can drag between them and watch a change land in plan, section and 3D simultaneously. Pair with Close Inactive Views first, or you will tile every view you have ever opened.

name: Tab Views
description: Returns tiled views to a single tabbed window arrangement. The everyday counterpart to Tile Views when the comparison session is over.

name: Close Inactive Views
description: Closes every open view except the active one (and one per other open project). Run it periodically — dozens of open views quietly drag performance down on big models.

name: Hide Element (Temporary)
description: Temporarily hides the selected elements in the current view, marked by a cyan border until reset. Ideal for getting clutter out of the way mid-task without touching permanent visibility settings.

name: Isolate Element (Temporary)
description: Temporarily hides everything except the selected elements, perfect for working on one system in a dense view. The isolation lasts until reset or the view is closed — it never affects printing once reset.

name: Hide Category (Temporary)
description: Temporarily hides the whole category of the selected element — pick one tag and all tags vanish. Quicker than opening Visibility/Graphics for a momentary declutter.

name: Isolate Category (Temporary)
description: Temporarily shows only the categories of the selected elements, hiding all others. Useful for auditing a single category — every room, every column — without building a filter.

name: Reset Temporary Hide/Isolate
description: Clears all temporary hide and isolate states in the view, removing the cyan border. Run it before printing or issuing — temporary states are per-session and easy to forget about.

name: Hide in View
description: Permanently hides the selected elements in the current view until deliberately unhidden. Use it for genuine per-view decisions — and Reveal Hidden Elements to find things again when a drawing looks mysteriously empty.

name: Hide Category in View
description: Permanently switches off the selected element's whole category in this view, equivalent to unticking it in Visibility/Graphics. Handy for one-off views; use templates when many views need the same treatment.

name: Unhide Element
description: Restores a permanently hidden element to visibility, used while Reveal Hidden Elements mode is active. The partner command VU does the same for whole categories.

name: Reveal Hidden Elements
description: Toggles a mode that shows everything hidden in the view in magenta so it can be selected and unhidden. The go-to diagnostic when content you know exists refuses to appear in a view.

name: Section Box
description: Crops a 3D view to a resizable box, slicing the model open to expose interiors and junctions. Enable it in the 3D view's properties, then drag the arrows — invaluable for design reviews and detail investigation.

name: Crop View
description: Limits a view to a rectangular (or sketch-edited) boundary, with a separate annotation crop for text and tags. Turn the crop region on to frame exactly what a sheet should show and nothing more.

name: View Range
description: Defines the horizontal slice a plan view cuts through — cut plane, top, bottom and view depth. The usual suspect when something on a level refuses to show: check whether it falls outside the range before anything else.

name: Zoom in Region
description: Zooms into a rectangular region you drag on screen. One of a family of zoom shortcuts worth learning early, alongside scroll-wheel zoom and pan.

name: Zoom to Fit
description: Zooms the active view out to show everything it contains. The quick recovery move when you have lost your bearings deep in a detail.

name: Zoom All to Fit
description: Zooms every open view to fit its contents at once, most useful straight after tiling views for a comparison session. Saves fitting each tile by hand.

name: Materials
description: Opens the material browser where appearance, graphics, identity and physical assets are defined and assigned. Materials drive hatching, rendering and schedules alike, so curate a tidy library rather than duplicating on the fly.

name: Object Styles
description: Sets the project-wide default line weights, colours and patterns for every category and subcategory. This is the base graphics standard that Visibility/Graphics then overrides per view — get it right once, in the template.

name: Project Units
description: Sets display units, rounding and symbols for length, area, angle and every other measured quantity. Display only — the database stays exact — but wrong rounding on issued drawings is an avoidable embarrassment.

name: Project Information
description: Edits project-wide data — client, project name, number, address — that title blocks read automatically. Fill it in at project setup so every sheet is labelled from one source of truth.

name: Project Parameters
description: Adds custom parameters to chosen categories across the whole project — a fire rating on doors, a room finish code. Project parameters schedule but cannot appear in tags; use shared parameters when tagging is needed.

name: Shared Parameters
description: Manages the external text file of parameter definitions shared between families, projects and offices. The mechanism behind taggable, schedulable custom data — guard the file carefully, as its GUIDs are what make parameters match.

name: Global Parameters
description: Defines project-level values that can drive dimensions and element parameters — a standard corridor width, a typical sill height. Change the value once and every constrained dimension follows, like family parameters at project scale.

name: Transfer Project Standards
description: Copies system settings — wall types, line styles, materials, fill patterns, view templates — from another open project into this one. The clean way to pull office standards or a colleague's types across without copy-pasting elements.

name: Purge Unused
description: Removes families, types and styles that nothing in the project references, shrinking file size and decluttering type selectors. Run it several times in a row — purging one item often orphans another.

name: Phases
description: Defines the project's time stages — existing, demolition, proposed — and the graphic overrides each phase filter applies. Every element and view carries phase settings, which is how one model produces existing, demo and proposed drawings.

name: Design Options
description: Maintains alternative design schemes inside one model — two entrance layouts, three facade studies — each shown in its own views. Accept the chosen option to merge it into the main model and discard the rest.

name: Worksets
description: Divides a workshared model into named chunks — shell, interiors, links — that users can own and views can filter. Beyond multi-user editing, worksets are a powerful visibility and performance lever on large models.

name: Synchronize with Central
description: Publishes your local changes to the central model and pulls everyone else's down, releasing borrowed elements as it goes. Sync regularly with a comment — long gaps between syncs make conflicts and lost work far more likely.

name: Collaborate
description: Enables worksharing on a model, either on a network as a central file or in the cloud for Revit Cloud Worksharing. The one-way door into multi-user working — agree workset structure before flicking the switch.

name: Copy/Monitor
description: Copies grids, levels or columns from a linked model and keeps watching them, flagging a coordination alert whenever the original moves. The formal handshake for shared datums between architect and engineer.

name: Interference Check
description: Runs a clash test between chosen categories, in the model or against a link, and reports overlapping pairs. A useful in-Revit first pass before dedicated clash tools like Navisworks take over.

name: Path of Travel
description: Calculates the shortest route between two points in plan, dodging modelled obstacles, and draws it with its length. Built for escape-distance and circulation checks that update as the plan changes.

name: Extrusion
description: Creates solid geometry in a family by pushing a sketched profile straight out to a depth. The first form tool to learn — most joinery, casework and simple components are little more than well-parameterised extrusions.

name: Blend
description: Creates a solid that morphs between two different profiles, a base and a top, over its height. Use it for tapering forms — hoppers, plinths, transitional fittings — that a single-profile extrusion cannot make.

name: Revolve
description: Spins a sketched profile around an axis to create a solid of revolution — balusters, domes, columns, bowls. Sketch the profile and axis on the same work plane, then set the sweep angle.

name: Sweep
description: Runs a profile along a sketched or picked path to form a solid — skirtings, handrails, gutters, cornices. Keep the profile sketch simple and the path clean; tight bends smaller than the profile will fail.

name: Swept Blend
description: Sweeps along a path while morphing between two end profiles, combining sweep and blend in one form. The tool for tapering rails, transitions and sculptural mouldings.

name: Void Forms
description: Creates negative geometry — void extrusions, blends, revolves, sweeps — that carves material away from solid forms. The standard way to cut rebates, holes and recesses in family geometry, paired with Cut Geometry in the project.

name: Reference Line
description: Draws a finite construction line with its own work planes, used to drive angular behaviour in families — an adjustable lamp arm, a flip-up seat. Unlike reference planes, reference lines rotate cleanly, making them the skeleton for moving parts.

name: Family Types
description: Opens the dialog where a family's parameters and named types are defined, with values and formulas per type. This is where flexing happens — change values here to test that the geometry behaves before loading into a project.

name: Family Category and Parameters
description: Assigns the family to a Revit category and sets behaviours like work-plane-based or shared. Category choice controls tagging, scheduling and visibility for every future instance, so decide it before modelling, not after.

name: Load into Project
description: Pushes the family you are editing straight into an open project, offering to overwrite the existing version and its parameter values. The tight edit-load-test loop that makes family development fast.

name: New Family
description: Starts a new loadable family from a category template — the template choice fixes hosting behaviour and category, so pick deliberately. Generic Model templates are the flexible fallback when no specific template fits.

name: Edit Family
description: Opens the selected instance's family in the Family Editor for modification. Combined with Load into Project, this is the round trip for fixing content without hunting for the source RFA on disk.

name: Properties
description: Toggles the Properties palette showing instance parameters of the selection, or the active view when nothing is selected. Keep it docked permanently — view properties in particular are edited here constantly.

name: Type Properties
description: Opens the parameters shared by every instance of the selected type — wall build-ups, frame materials, panel sizes. Edits here change all instances at once, so duplicate the type first when only some should change.

name: Project Browser
description: The tree of every view, legend, schedule, sheet, family and group in the project — double-click to open, right-click to duplicate, rename or delete. Customise its sorting and filtering on large jobs to keep hundreds of views navigable.

name: Keyboard Shortcuts
description: Opens the dialog for viewing, assigning and exporting keyboard shortcuts for almost any command. Ten minutes personalising shortcuts for your most-used tools pays back daily.
